Name: Lo-Ammi
Summary: Lo-Ammi (KJV 'Lo-ammi'), son of Hosea and Gomer, was named by God as a sign: his name means 'not my people,' declaring that Israel had broken covenant so deeply that God would disown them as His people — a judgment later reversed in the promise that they would be called sons of the living God.
KeyStory: God named Hosea's son Lo-Ammi — 'not my people' — the hardest of the three sign-names, announcing the breaking of the covenant bond.
LifeLesson: Lo-Ammi's name is the darkest sentence in Hosea — and the reason the book's ending shines: the God who says 'not my people' also promises to say 'my people' again.
